output.title: When date ambiguity stops working
output.body:
If you run a small business, date ambiguity is only a problem when it keeps interrupting the same workflow. The question is not whether AI can read a date. It is whether your team keeps losing time to missing timezones, mixed date formats, or two systems that disagree on the same deadline.

The practical decision is simple: keep checking dates by hand, hire someone to watch the queue, or use a bounded automation that standardises dates at the point of entry and flags unclear cases before they spread. That is a fit check, not a promise. If every date comes from one place in one format, the problem may be small. If dates arrive from email, forms, spreadsheets, and memory, the mess will keep inventing itself. Very considerate, in a hostile way.

One useful next step is to watch a single recurring workflow for a week and count each time date ambiguity forces a pause, clarification, or correction. Ask: how often does a missing timezone or conflicting date source stop the work? If the same confusion keeps appearing, you have a repeatable control problem. Then the owner can decide whether a bounded fix is worth the effort, with human approval still in charge where the stakes are high.
